title: test(service-automation): keep the DST-offset clocked windows empty of setup
body:
Fixes #19768

Clause-②: no

`template-date-offset-dst.test.ts` timed out at 5000 ms on `Test Core (3/6)` on an
unrelated PR. This PR takes the setup out of the clocked windows. It does not widen the
budget, and it reports — with numbers — that the budget was never the binding constraint.

## Premise check, done first on `origin/main`

The card's own facts hold: the file is exactly where the card says it is (the body writes
the path without its `packages/` prefix), every `it()` goes through `at()` at `:70`, and
`at()` sets `process.env.TZ`, installs a fake `Date` and restores both. `premise_still_valid: true`.

The card's explicitly-unmeasured **hypothesis** does not hold, and the rest of this
section is the measurement that refutes it.

## What the clocked window actually contains

Every case in this file is **synchronous** and performs no I/O, no module resolution and
no `await`. `interpolateString` is a static top-level import; the date branch it exercises
(`template.ts:212-242`) is one regex plus `setUTCDate`/`toISOString`.

That matters because of how the verdict is reached. In `@vitest/runner` 4.1.11,
`runWithTimeout` starts a real `setTimeout` and **also** re-checks the clock on the
resolve path:

```js
const startTime = now();             // performance.now, not the faked Date
...
function resolve(result) {
  clearTimeout(timer);
  // if test/hook took too long in microtask, setTimeout won't be triggered,
  // but we still need to fail the test
  if (now() - startTime >= timeout) { rejectTimeoutError(); return; }
```

A synchronous body cannot be interrupted by that timer — the macrotask cannot run while
the body holds the thread — so on **this** file the message can only ever have come from
the post-hoc branch. "Test timed out in 5000 ms" here means *the wall clock advanced 5 s
while a synchronous body ran*, never *the test waited for something*.

So the question is what that body costs. Measured on this container, one `at()` per case,
cold, exactly as the file runs them:

| case (cold, one draw each) | window |
|:---|---:|
| first case (`America/New_York`, also paying the JIT) | 2.343 ms |
| the other thirteen cells | 0.154 – 0.384 ms |

Against a 5000 ms budget that is roughly **13,000x of headroom**. Warm, with N = 200 draws
per step, the five steps of `at()` break down as:

| step | p50 | max | share of total |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|
| `process.env.TZ = zone` | 0.011 ms | 0.143 ms | 13% |
| `vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ['Date'] })` | 0.023 ms | 1.140 ms | 34% |
| `vi.setSystemTime(...)` | 0.006 ms | 0.121 ms | 8% |
| the assertions themselves | 0.013 ms | 0.549 ms | 20% |
| `vi.useRealTimers()` + TZ restore | 0.019 ms | 0.269 ms | 23% |
| **whole `at()` window** | **0.076 ms** | **2.230 ms** | |

## The card's hypothesis, measured and refuted

The card guessed that "the first cell to enter a given zone may pay a zone-data load" and
said plainly that it had not timed one. It is a real effect and it is four orders of
magnitude too small. Warming the code first on one zone (500 draws), then entering 30
zones never seen in the process, then re-entering the same 30:

| | p50 | p90 | max |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|
| first use of a zone | 0.025 ms | 0.113 ms | 0.679 ms |
| repeat use of the same zone | 0.014 ms | 0.019 ms | 0.024 ms |

~0.011 ms at the median. It is also **not** load-sensitive in the way the prior art's
module resolution was: repeating both passes under six concurrent
`find node_modules -type f` loops left first-use at p50 0.025 ms / max 0.131 ms.

## What does explain a 5000 ms window

A whole-process stall — and one of that shape reproduces here. Under the same six
filesystem-walk loops, the 500 warm single-zone draws that read **p50 0.005 ms / max
0.056 ms** on a quiet box drew a **max of 4.058 ms**: an 800x stretch of a window that
performs no I/O at all. The shard that filed this card was importing 498 s of modules in
193 s of wall clock while `@objectstack/cli:build`, `@objectstack/verify:build` and
`@objectstack/runtime:test` ran alongside it.

⛔ A stall cannot be repaired from inside a test file, and this PR does not claim to have
repaired one. What can be reduced is the **exposed window**, which is what the budget is
actually spent on.

## The change

Two constructs, both of them setup rather than the behaviour this file pins, leave the
clocked window:

1. **The fake `Date` now belongs to the file** — `beforeAll` installs it, `afterAll`
   removes it. Every case in this file wants the identical fake, and the install/uninstall
   pair was 57% of the warm window. It mattered most where it is least visible: six of the
   27 cases are aggregates that call `at()` 11 to 14 times, so each of those windows was
   paying the pair 11 to 14 times.
2. **Every zone is entered once at module load**, before any clocked window exists, so no
   case is the first user of a zone. This is the small effect measured above. It is kept
   because it is *loading*, and this repo's rule is that a clocked window measures
   behaviour, never loading — not because the fix leans on it.

`setSystemTime` stays inside `at()`: it is the part that carries the cell's instant.

## `process.env.TZ` is process-global — what guarantees no other test sees a mutated TZ

Unchanged by this PR, and stated because the question is the right one:

- `at()` restores TZ in a `finally`, so a failing assertion leaves nothing behind; the
  module-load warm-up restores it on its own last line; and the file's final fence
  asserts `process.env.TZ === REAL_TZ` directly.
- The window in which TZ is mutated is **synchronous**, so nothing else in this worker can
  observe it: tests in a file run sequentially and none here is `concurrent`.
- Measured, not assumed: this suite runs on vitest's default `forks` pool
  (`isMainThread=true`, `threadId=0`), and two test files in one `vitest run` reported
  **different pids** (4804, 4805) — each file gets its own child process, so `process.env`
  is that file's own copy and not a store shared with sibling workers.

The one thing this PR does change is that the fake `Date` is now installed for the whole
file rather than per case. That is contained by the same boundary: the fake lives in that
file's own process and `afterAll` removes it.

## Before / after — same command, N named, reported per case

The failure is a wall-clock verdict, so the reproduction scales the **budget down** rather
than scaling the load up. Same file, same command, same box, both sides:

```
pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation exec vitest run --testTimeout=2 src/builtin/template-date-offset-dst.test.ts
```

N = 10 runs per side, quiet box. "before" is this file at `HEAD~1`, restored into the same
worktree and hash-verified against the `HEAD~1` blob, then restored to `HEAD` and verified
again (`git diff HEAD` empty).

| | timeouts | where they landed |
|:---|---:|:---|
| before | **18** | 10 on the first cell; 3 + 3 + 1 on three aggregate fences (14, 12 and 11 `at()` calls); 1 on a single-cell case |
| after | **11** | 10 on the first cell; 1 on one aggregate fence |

The aggregate cases are the reading that names the construct: **8 timeouts to 1**. The
residual carries its own control — the first cell times out 10 of 10 on **both** sides,
because at a 2 ms budget it is the scaled harness's own cold-start floor (2.343 ms
measured above), not this construct. It is reported, not papered over.

At a tighter budget the same ordering holds, and it survives contention: N = 10 per side at
`--testTimeout=1`, before 70 timeouts / after 43 on a quiet box, before 70 / after 50 under
the six filesystem-walk loops.

Per case at the real budget, from vitest's own reporter (1 ms resolution, N = 3 runs per
side, same command both sides):

| case | before | after |
|:---|:---|:---|
| first cell | 5, 5, 5 ms | 3, 3, 3 ms |
| `bare {TODAY()}` fence (14 `at()`) | 2, 2, 2 ms | 1, 1, 1 ms |
| `zones that do not observe DST` (12 `at()`) | 2, 2, 2 ms | 1, 1, 1 ms |
| `an ordinary instant in a DST zone` (11 `at()`) | 2, 2, 2 ms | 1, 1, 1 ms |
| `bare {NOW()}` fence (11 `at()`) | 1, 1, 2 ms | 1, 1, 1 ms |
| `both directions are represented` (14 `at()`) | 1, 1, 2 ms | 1, 1, 1 ms |
| whole file, vitest's `tests` total | 25, 24, 26 ms | 20, 20, 19 ms |

## What was deliberately not done

No `.skip`, no `.todo`, no quarantine, no deletion, no `retry`, no flaky-tolerance, and
`testTimeout` is untouched. The work needs a fraction of a millisecond, so a bigger number
would record a property of the machine as if it were a property of this test. ⛔ Nothing in
`src/engine.test.ts` was touched. ⛔ Nothing in `packages/spec` was touched. No symbol is
exported and no assertion changed: the 14 measured red cells, their inline disagree-first
controls, and every fence are byte-identical.

## Verification, at `479a8271fa`

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation test` — `Test Files 141 passed (141)`,
  `Tests 1690 passed (1690)`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation run typecheck` — clean;
  `check:test-typecheck: OK`, 0 files / 0 errors.
- Dependency closure built first: `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/service-automation^...' build`.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --ran` —
  `53 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 53 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED`, every one exit 0. Two of
  them (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:type-check-debt`) first answered
  `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` at exit 3 on an unbuilt workspace, which is not a finding; they
  were re-run at exit 0 after
  `pnpm exec turbo run build --filter='./packages/*' --filter='./packages/*/*'`.
- `pnpm lint` (`eslint . --no-inline-config`, the whole repo, not a narrowing) — exit 0,
  read before any pipe, at `479a8271fa`.

## Changeset

`skip-changeset`, and it is the *diff publishes nothing* case, not the "no changeset
needed" shrug. The diff is one `*.test.ts` file. `@objectstack/service-automation`'s
`files[]` is `dist`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`; after
`pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation build`, each of `warmZoneData`,
`NON_DST_FENCE_ZONES`, `mixedCalendarSpelling` and `DST_CELLS` has **zero** hits under
`dist/`, while the positive controls `interpolateString` and `resolveToken` hit two
emitted artifacts each. No published byte changes, so an empty changeset would be a false
declaration rather than a neutral one.

## Acceptance notes

- This file costs 4.2 s of `import` and 3.4 s of `transform` locally to reach one function,
  `interpolateString`, and the shard that filed the card spent 498 s of its 193 s wall clock
  importing. That is outside every clocked window and is not this card; noted, not filed.
- The two aggregate fences each re-enter all 14 cells inside one `it()`, so a failure in
  them names no cell. Diagnostic shape only, no defect; noted, not filed.
